payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear comparison of segmentation performance between words and morphemes, indicating that different supervision levels affect the results.

claims.text: Segmentation metrics are better with morpheme-based references in unsupervised settings, while word-based annotations yield better metrics in supervised settings.
With morpheme supervision, there is an improvement in word segmentation, but not for morpheme boundaries, indicating a complexity in segmentation processes.
The results suggest that a naive view of segmentation, considering only one type of boundary, is insufficient for fully utilizing annotated data.
